Adding a second SQL Server 2022 node to the cluster

  • This section describes how to add a node to the SQL Server 2022 failover clustered instance on a multisubnet Windows Server Failover Cluster. The installation process is run on the second node of the cluster, SQLNODE-02.

    To add a node on a SQL Server 2022 multisubnet failover clustered instance:

    1. Run setup.exe from the installation media to launch SQL Server Installation Center.
    2. Click the Installation link on the bottom left. Click the Add node to a SQL Server failover cluster link. This runs the SQL Server 2022 Setup wizard.
    3. In the Product Key dialog box, enter the product key that came with your installation media and click Next.
    4. In the License Terms dialog box, click the I accept the license terms check box and click Next.
    5. In the Global Rules dialog box, validate that the checks return successful results and click Next.
    6. In the Microsoft Update dialog box, click Next.
    7. In the Add Node Rules dialog box, validate that the checks return successful results. If the checks returned a few warnings, make sure you fix them before proceeding with the installation. Click Next.
    8. In the Cluster Node Configuration dialog box, validate that the information for the existing SQL Server 2022 failover clustered instance is correct. Click Next.
    9. In the Cluster Network Configuration dialog box, enter the virtual IP address and subnet mask that the SQL Server 2022 failover cluster instance will use in the network subnet that the second node is in – 10.65.128.0/18. Notice that the setup process also detected the existence of two network subnets. Since the virtual IP address for the 10.65.64.0/18 subnet has already been configured, that option has been disabled.
    10. In the Service Accounts dialog box, verify that the information is the same that was used to configure the first node. Click Next.
    11. In the Feature Rules dialog box, click Next.
    12. In the Ready to Add Node dialog box, verify that all configurations are correct and click Install.
    13. Once the installation finishes, in the Complete dialog box, click Close. This concludes adding a node to a SQL Server 2022 multisubnet Cluster.

Adding a third SQL Server node on a SQL Server 2022 multi-subnet cluster

    1. Run the setup.exe file from the installation media to launch the SQL Server Installation Center. 
    2. Click the Installation link on the bottom left. Click the Add node to a SQL Server failover cluster link. This runs the SQL Server 2022 Setup wizard. 
    3. In the Product Key dialog box, enter the product key that came with your installation media and click Next. 
    4. In the License Terms dialog box, click the I accept the license terms check box and click Next. 
    5. In the Global Rules dialog box, validate that the checks return successful results and click Next. 
    6. In the Microsoft Update dialog box, click Next. 
    7. In the Add Node Rules dialog box, validate that the checks return successful results. If the checks returned a few warnings, make sure you fix them before proceeding with the installation. Click Next. 
    8. In the Cluster Node Configuration dialog box, validate that the information for the existing SQL Server 2022 failover clustered instance is correct. Click Next. 
    9. In the Cluster Network Configuration dialog box, enter the virtual IP address and subnet mask that the SQL Server 2022 failover cluster instance will use in the network subnet that the third node is in 10.65.32.0/19. Notice that the setup process also detected the existence of three network subnets. Since the virtual IP address for the 10.65.64.0/18 and 10.65.128.0/18 subnet has already been configured, that option has been disabled. 
    10. In the Service Accounts dialog box, verify that the information is the same as what was used to configure the first node. Click Next. 
    11. In the Feature Rules dialog box, click Next. 
    12. In the Ready to Add Node dialog box, verify that all configurations are correct and click Install. 
    13. Once the installation finishes, in the Complete dialog box. 


    The SQL Server 2022 multisubnet failover cluster node addition is now complete.

Architecture

  • The APEX Block Storage deployment contains instances that may or may not be physical machines, depending on the type of instance selected. 

    For the deployment, the management stack includes APEX Block Storage Manager, the proxy server, and the temporary management platform installer. 

    APEX Block Storage does not include SDCs (the consumers of storage). The customer is responsible for deploying the compute instances on AWS instances of their choice.

Conclusion

  • Dell APEX Block Storage for Public Cloud enables customers to easily deploy and run their workloads in the cloud. Dell APEX Block Storage for Public Cloud can be deployed across multiple availability zones and supports both EBS-based volumes that offer persistence and native NVMe SSD drives for increased performance. Using the APEX Block Storage two-layer software defined infrastructure design, customers can deploy and scale both APEX Block Storage and compute nodes independently to match the growth demands of their critical workloads.

    SQL Server 2022 multisubnet failover cluster on Amazon EC2 instances provides improved availability and disaster recovery capabilities for SQL Server deployments. This paper demonstrates how SQL Server 2022 failover clusters can be configured across availability zones with Dell APEX Block Storage for Public Cloud and showcases the performance that can be achieved with SQL Server databases running on Dell APEX Block Storage for Public Cloud.

Dell APEX Block Storage components

  • The fundamental building blocks of an APEX Block Storage solution are: 

    MDM – Meta Data Manager – The brains of the storage layer 

    • Oversees storage cluster configuration, monitoring, rebalancing, and rebuilding 
    • A highly available, independent cluster installed on three or five different nodes 
    • May reside alongside SDCs and/or SDSs or on separate instances 
    • Located outside the data path 

    SDR – Storage Data Replicator 

    • Handles replication activities between Dell APEX Block Storage systems 
    • Located alongside the SDS on the same node 
    • Highly available. If failure occurs, the MDM instructs the SDC to send data to alternative SDRs. 
    • The Source journals incoming writes and ships them to the target 
    • The Target receives the journal and applies it to the target volumes 

     SDC – Storage Data Client (Consumer of storage) 

    • Provides front-end volume access to applications and file systems 
    • Installed on instances that are consuming storage 
    • Maintains peer-to-peer connections to every SDS managing a pool of storage 
    • Understands how to make read and write requests to different parts of the system 

    SDS – Storage Data Server (Supplier of storage) 

    • Abstracts local storage, maintains storage pools, and presents volumes to the SDCs 
    • Installed on instances that contribute local disks to the storage cluster 
    • A protection domain is a collection of SDS instances 
    • Manages the data that is spread evenly across all the contributing nodes in the cluster. This provides the opportunity for massively parallel processing. 

    APEX Block Storage for AWS management instances (MDM and MDM tiebreaker), Secure Connect Gateway (SCG), APEX Block Storage Manager Platform, and proxy server instances use AWS EBS gp3 volumes exclusively.

Dell APEX Block Storage for Public Cloud

  • For decades, the enterprise infrastructure industry has been optimizing ways for architectural ingredients to interoperate. Storage that meets the needs of discriminating enterprise requirements is a core competency of the Dell Technologies portfolio. Taking advantage of these capabilities, while embracing the agility afforded by cloud infrastructure, brings together the best of both worlds. 

    As a market leading supplier of software-defined storage, we enable outcomes on the public cloud that take scale, performance, and durability to an outstanding level. This document describes how to bring your enterprise storage experience to the cloud to meet the most demanding needs of your mission-critical applications. 

    To truly embrace multicloud, there is also a fundamental need for storage as a service (STaaS) based management and orchestration. The Dell APEX Navigator experience solves for and manage day zero deployments and day two management of all Dell software-defined cloud storage and data protection endpoints. Optionally, support for Kubernetes storage management can also be delivered as part of this solution. 

    Native hyperscaler solution offerings can achieve three to four nines of availability. These solutions rely on zone-redundant replication to replicate services around to protect solutions from single points of failure. With Dell APEX Block Storage, we use the native offering instance but take the resiliency many steps forward. The offering can span multiple availability zones with a single cluster. The offering also deploys its own highly available metadata management, as part of the mesh-mirror architecture. This vastly improves resiliency and reliability over and above native hyperscaler offerings. 

    To make a solid business case for Dell APEX Block storage, we must provide proven on-premises performance, scale, and resiliency, coupled with seamless data mobility and monitoring. These enterprise features can be deployed easily, and with little friction, to multiple hyperscalers. As a result, you can now place the right data, in the right location, at the right time, for the right consumption service. 

    The scale out software-defined architecture enables extreme performance by aggregating storage resources and distributing the data access across the cluster to deliver large IOPS with low latency. Aggregating the resources with the solution’s SDS results in performance that is the sum of the component pieces' performance. 

    One can rapidly expand the cluster to increase both performance and capacity while maintaining low latency. Each additional instance adds additional I/O and capacity to the cluster, with up to 512 nodes in a single deployment. This enables extreme performance and capacity. 

    If you choose to deploy Dell APEX Block Storage directly to instances backed with general purpose disks, Dell APEX Block Storage can aggregate the shared storage resources of the lower performing and cost-effective disks to achieve higher performance and resilience than native cloud offerings.

Dell APEX Block Storage for Public Cloud

  • How can we achieve this?

    The solution aggregates the resources and then shares them across the entire cluster. APEX Block Storage then automatically maintains a balance across all resources, to support each application’s need. You can also add storage and/or compute on-the-fly with no downtime or impact to applications because APEX Block Storage seamlessly balances the available resources.

    The same flexibility exists with Dell APEX Block Storage for other hyperscalers. The software can be deployed on either managed disks for most workloads or on instances with native attached NVMe SSDs for more performance optimized workloads. A deployment of Dell APEX Block can provide these benefits:

    • Flexible deployments: Provide options to optimize cost and performance based on your workload requirements.
    • Seamless data mobility: Dell APEX Block Storage offers several ways to move data from on premises to the cloud and back, and between regions in the cloud. Features include native asynchronous replication, snapshots, and integrated backup and recovery solutions. Dell APEX Navigator for Multicloud Storage orchestrates data mobility capabilities, such as snapshot shipping, in a coming release of APEX Navigator.
    • Multi-AZ durability: Dell APEX Block Storage has a unique ability to spread data protection across multi-availability zones, ensuring data access without having extra copies of data or needing to use replication across AZs.
    • Enterprise data services: The product provides thin provisioning, snapshots, and replication which can be required for mission-critical workloads on the public clouds. Dell APEX Block Storage native replication enables data mobility between on-premises and cloud and/or to have a warm standby copy in another region or on-premises for additional protection against a regional disaster.
    • Performance and linear scalability: Dell APEX Block Storage is well suited to support large databases, analytics workloads, and multiple container (Kubernetes) development and production deployments.
    • The cloud experience – anywhere: Being able to access and interact with cloud services, resources, and applications from anywhere, regardless of the physical location of the data.

    Organizations today have data and applications spread across multiple data centers, co-location facilities, public clouds, and increasingly at the edge. Customers enjoy the ease and agility of the cloud experience and are demanding this same experience across all their deployments. Simply put, this is the business case for Dell APEX Block Storage for Public Cloud—the cloud experience that is seamlessly delivered wherever organizations have data and applications. 

    To successfully deliver the business use case to end users, the APEX Block Storage solution provides these benefits. 

    Best of breed innovation:

    • Cloud native storage built for cloud native development. 
    • Storage innovation where it is needed, extending existing IT investments and skill sets. 

    Data mobility: 

    • Mobility is geared toward both those who already have a PowerFlex on-premises environment and want to migrate to the cloud, and those who have already deployed Dell APEX Block Storage in the cloud and want to move data among various Dell APEX Block Storage deployments. 
    • Consume the public cloud PaaS services, with only the data attributes that you want, in the cloud. 
    • Consume the rich hyperscaler PaaS feature set reporting capability by mounting volumes copied from on-premises locations. 
    • Allowing for seamless data mobility, data teams can now place the right data, at the right time, in the right place. 
    • Snapshot shipping of volumes to the hyperscaler ecosystem to provide a source for, and to enhance, AI/ML model training. 
    • Consume what you need in the hyperscaler of choice, without incurring any egress fees. 
    • Copy and mount snapshots in the cloud. 
    • Kubernetes namespace data mobility. Inclusive of all PV and PVCs, with an option to rename a namespace in flight. 
    • Evolving S3 Object solution sets as a query able source for a modern database system. 
    • NOSQL databases – Develop in the cloud. Migrate to on-premises or other cloud. Following the no lock in pattern of NOSQL distributed systems. 

    Ease of deployment and provisioning: 

    • Complete automated deployment in less than two hours when deployed with APEX Navigator 
    • Scaling without physical hardware acquisition channels 
    • Network automation 
    • Code upgrades for the APEX Block Storage software defined solution 
    • Custom deployment guidance: 
    • Step-by-step instructions for manually adding to an existing Dell APEX Block Storage infrastructure. 
    • Support for use cases is not addressed by the orchestrated APEX Navigator deployment option. 

    Fully automated experience with APEX Navigator: 

    • Centralize APEX Block Storage deployment and life cycle management across multiple public clouds, including configuration and automated provisioning and deployment. This process requires only four simple steps. 
    • Drive data mobility between on-premises and multiple public clouds to meet shifting cloud strategies. 
    • API-first architecture makes it easy to integrate with automation tools such as Ansible and Terraform to accelerate productivity and embrace Dell software defined storage in the public cloud as part of your broader IT strategy. 
    • Take decisive action with intelligent insights to leverage comprehensive monitoring across your entire Dell storage estate. You can also track license inventory, system health, performance, and capacity with CloudIQ integration. 
    • Accelerate Zero Trust adoption with role-based access control, single sign-on, and federated identity, all leveraging Zero Trust principles. 

    APEX Block Storage for Public Cloud also offers: 

    • The ability to achieve extreme performance in the public cloud. 
    • Linear scalability to 100 s of storage instances to address large workloads and to consolidate large sets of applications in one cloud. 
    • APEX Block Storage for Public Cloud can be consumed by thousands of compute instances. 
    • Rapid deployment through an intelligent web-based wizard that removes the complexity of finding which instances best fit the workload and the capacity required. The solution supports the expansion and monitoring of your capacity, as needed. 
    • A unique use of Availability Zones which, mapped to fault sets, enable high resiliency with a space-efficient and cost-effective use of the distributed mesh data across the data store. This entails enabling ultrafast reprotection of an entire AZ that could go offline without disrupting access to your Dell APEX Block Storage. 
    • A choice of running block-based cloud storage on either EBS volumes or an EC2 instance store for performance optimized workloads.

Dell APEX Block Storage for Public Cloud

  • Consider the following recommendations for the Dell APEX Block Storage for Public Cloud:

    • Deploying APEX Block Storage in multiple Availability Zones (AZs) can mitigate workload downtime if an AZ becomes unavailable. When availability is not critical, APEX Block Storage deployment can also be done in a single AZ.
    • For APEX Block Storage clusters with applications that are planned to be used 24x7, it is recommended to use the i3en EC2 instance family with NVMe SSDs optimized for low latency and high I/O performance. Instance store disks are ephemeral, and their data is deleted when the instances are stopped (this does not include reboots).
    • For APEX Block Storage clusters with applications that are frequently brought down (such as for holidays and weekends), consider using c5n EC2 instances with EBS volumes. While they lack the performance of NVMe SSDs, their data remains persistent even when the APEX Block Storage cluster nodes are stopped.
    • Use a public subnet for external-facing resources that communicate with the Internet.
    • Use a private subnet for internal resources that does not communicate with the Internet.

Executive summary

  • Running mission-critical applications in the public cloud is gaining popularity as businesses adopt the benefits of cloud operations, including agility, ease of use, security, a robust set of software tools and services, and dynamic scale.

    Dell APEX Block Storage for Public Cloud brings to the public cloud the advantages of scale, performance, and a robust feature set, including local and remote replication, high availability (HA), resiliency, and CloudIQ security.

    Dell APEX Block Storage for Public Cloud can be rapidly deployed through a web portal that automates the initial deployment, or to expand an existing system, making the process simple and quick. The scale-out design allows for independent storage and compute instances that can be spread across AWS Availability Zones (AZs), providing higher resiliency if an AZ is down. Dell APEX Block Storage for Public Cloud provides a choice of Elastic Block Storage (EBS) for more flexibility, or native attached NVMe SSD drives for increased performance.

    Some of the advantages of deploying applications with APEX Block Storage in AWS include:

    • Extreme performance: APEX Block Storage native storage resiliency allows the use of local NVMe disks (AWS instance store) which provides higher IOPS and lower latency for mission-critical applications compared to native cloud virtual disks.
    • Improved resiliency: When the APEX Block Storage cluster is configured across AWS AZs, even when one AZ is down, the data continues to be available for operations to resume in other AZs.
    • Uniform experience: Whether APEX Block Storage software is deployed on-premises or public clouds, it is the same software. As a result, the same knowledge and deployment models that are built in one environment can be used in another, creating ease of use and faster ability to deploy applications anywhere.
    • SQL Server databases that are deployed on APEX Block Storage in AWS give customers full control over the infrastructure components and database environment. You can also use APEX Block Storage capabilities like replication and snapshots while managing and monitoring the APEX Block Storage system. All the components, including Amazon EC2 instances, storage volumes, scalability, and security, may be configured and tuned using this flexible design of APEX Block Storage in accordance with AWS best practices.

    This white paper explains the best practices and performance benefits of running SQL Server 2022 failover clusters and databases on Dell APEX Block Storage for Public Cloud.

Failover cluster validation wizard

  • This section describes how to run the Failover Cluster Validation Wizard from the Failover Cluster Management console. You can launch the tool from the Server Manager dashboard, under Tools and select Failover Cluster Manager. 

    Note: These steps can be performed on any of the servers that act as nodes in your failover cluster. The steps below are performed on SQLNODE-01.

    1. In the Failover Cluster Management console, under the Management section, click the Validate Configuration link. This runs the Validate a Configuration Wizard. 

    1. In the Select Servers or a Cluster dialog box, enter the hostnames of the nodes that you want to add as members of your cluster. Click Next. 

    1. In the Testing Options dialog box, click Next to run all the necessary tests to validate whether the nodes are ready for clustering. 

    1. In the Confirmation dialog box, click Next. This runs all the necessary validation tests. 

    1. In the Summary dialog box, verify that all the reports are successful. Click Finish to create the Windows Server Failover Cluster.

Install Dell APEX Block Storage SDC

  • The following steps describe the installation of Dell APEX Block Storage SDC component on all the Windows Server 2022 that are used for the Cluster configuration:

    1. Download the EMC-ScaleIO-sdc*.msi and LIA software.
    2. Double-click EMC-ScaleIO LIA setup.
    3. Accept the terms in the license agreement and click Install.

    1. Type msiexec /i <SDC_PATH>.msi MDM_IP=<LIST_VIP_MDM_IPS>, where <SDC_PATH> is the path where the SDC installation package is located. The <LIST_VIP_MDM_IPS> is a comma-separated list of the MDM IP addresses or the virtual IP address of the MDM.
    2. Accept the terms in the license agreement and click Install.

    1. To complete the installation, click Finish

    For more information about SDC installation, see Install and configure a Windows-based compute-only node to PowerFlex.

Install Dell APEX Block Storage SDC

  • Initialize and format the Disks

    The following steps describe how to initialize and format the disks. You can launch the tool from the Server Manager dashboard, under Tools and select Computer Management.

    1. Expand Storage and select Disk Management. 
    2. Right-click any of the disks that you want to configure and select Online. Once the disk is brought online, it is now marked as Not Initialized.

    1. To initialize, right-click the disk and select Initialize Disk. The Initialize Disk dialog box appears. 
    2. In the Initialize Disk dialog box, make sure that the correct disk is selected for initialization and then choose whether to initialize the disk using the MBR or GPT partition styles Click OK. 
    3. To create a disk partition, right-click the unallocated space and select New Simple Volume.
    4. In the Welcome to the New Simple Volume Wizard dialog box, click Next. 
    5. In the Specify Volume Size dialog box, enter the volume size and click Next. 
    6. In the Assign Drive Letter or Path dialog box, if using drive letters for the deployment specify the drive letter that you would like to use. Alternatively, select a mount-point for the volume, or do not assign either a mount-point or drive-letter if you plan to use the volume as CSV. Click Next. 
    7. In the Format Partition dialog box 
      1. Make sure that the file system selected is NTFS. 
      2. To follow Microsoft best practices on allocation unit size, select 64 K. 
      3. In the Volume label: Text box, enter the appropriate name.
      4. Click Next.

    1. In the New Simple Volume Wizard dialog box, review the settings that you have made, click Next and then click Finish.

Install SQL Server 2022

  • This section describes the installation of SQL Server 2022 failover clustered instance, which is integrated with Windows Server Failover Cluster. The installation process is run on the first node of cluster SQLNODE-01.

    1. Run setup.exe from the SQL Server 2022 installation media to launch SQL Server Installation Center. Click the Installation link on the bottom left side.
    2. Click the New SQL Server failover cluster installation link. This runs the SQL Server 2022 Setup wizard. 

    1. In the Product Key dialog box, enter the product key that came with your installation media and click Next. 
    2. In the License Terms dialog box, go through the license details and click the I accept the license terms check box and click Next. 
    3. In the Global Rules dialog box, validate that the checks return successful results and click Next. 
    4. In the Microsoft Update dialog box, click Next. In the Install Failover Cluster Rules dialog box, validate that the checks return successful results. If the checks returned a few warnings, make sure you fix them before proceeding with the installation. Click Next. 
    5. In the Setup Role dialog box, select the SQL Server Feature Installation option and click Next. 
    6. In the Feature Selection dialog box, select the following component: Database Engine Services and Click Next. 

    1. In the Feature Rules dialog box, verify that all the rules have passed. If the rules returned a few warnings, make sure you fix them before proceeding with the installation. Click Next. 
    2. In the Instance Configuration dialog box, for this example setup, the following parameters are entered: 
      • SQL Server Network Name: SQLFCI
      • Instance ID: SQLDBFCI

      Click Next.

    1. In the Cluster Resource Group dialog box, check the resources available on your Windows Server Failover Cluster. This tells you that a new Resource Group will be created on your cluster for the SQL Server instance. To specify the SQL Server cluster resource group name, you can either use the drop-down box to specify an existing group to use or type the name of a new group to create it. Accept all the defaults and click Next. 

    1. In the Cluster Disk Selection dialog box, select the available disks (the shared volumes mapped earlier to the Windows Server Failover Cluster nodes). These disks can be made available to SQL Server 2022 to use. Click Next. 

    1. In the Cluster Network Configuration dialog box, enter the virtual IP address and subnet mask that the SQL Server 2022 cluster will use. Notice that the setup process has detected the existence of multiple network subnets. 

    Select the checkbox beside the IPv4 column as a static IP address will be used and click Next.

    1. In the Server Configuration dialog box, set the credentials for the SQL Server service accounts in the Service Accounts tab. Make sure that both the SQL Server Agent and SQL Server Database Engine services have a Startup Type of Manual. SQL Full-text Filer Daemon Launcher and SQL Server Browser are build-in accounts that do not require a password. The Windows Server Failover Cluster takes care of stopping and starting the service. Also, set the Collation property for the instance according to your application requirement. Click Next.

    1. In the Database Engine Configuration dialog box, select the appropriate Authentication Mode in the Server Authentication tab. If you want to add the currently logged on user to be a part of the SQL Server administrators’ group, click the Add Current User button. Otherwise, you can add the appropriate domain accounts or security groups. 
    1.  In the Feature Configuration Rules dialog box click Next. 
    2.  In the Ready to Install dialog box, verify that all configurations are correct and click Next.

    1.  Once the installation finishes, in the Complete dialog box, click Close.

Logical architecture

  • The logical architecture described in this section shows the deployment of a three node SQL Server 2022 multisubnet failover cluster on Windows Server 2022 on a two-layer Dell APEX Block Storage configuration - SQL Server 2022 Node 1 in AZ-1a, SQL Server 2022 Node 2 in AZ-1b, and SQL Server 2022 Node 3 in AZ-1c. SQL Server setup classifies this configuration as a multisubnet cluster. The APEX Block Storage deployment across three AZs offers increased resiliency and availability.

    Figure 5 represents the two-layer APEX Block Storage system using the Amazon instance store (natively attached to NVMe SSD drives).

     Figure 5.                        Logical architecture of WFSC and SQL Server on APEX Block Storage using instance store.

    In each AZ, one SDS is installed on i3en.12xlarge Amazon EC2 instance with the Red Hat Enterprise Linux AMI. The Amazon EC2 instances that are deployed by APEX Block Storage in AWS are backed by NVMe SSD drives. The NVMe SSDs are locally attached at the Instance level. The natively attached NVMe SSD drives are ephemeral storage. There are three APEX Block Storage SDS instances that are configured into a single protection domain. A single storage pool is created, using all the storage devices available within the protection domain. 

    APEX Block Storage maintains the user data in a mesh mirrored layout such that each piece of data has two copies (primary and secondary) stored on two different storage optimized Amazon EC2 instances (SDS). The copies are evenly distributed across the SDS instances, which enables the system to maintain data availability and high-performance if there is a failure of a storage device or Amazon EC2 storage optimized instance. 

    The APEX Block Storage volumes that are created from the APEX Block Storage pool are mapped to Amazon EC2 compute instances running APEX Block Storage SDC services. The APEX Block Storage volumes mapped to instances are used to create the file system to host the databases.

Metadata communication

  • Within a deployed APEX Block Storage solution, only the SDS and the SDC exchange data. The MDM’s role is completely outside the data path. Its responsibility is to distribute cluster metadata about the data’s layout, about the storage cluster members (the SDS and SDCs), and to make sure that they are still operational. 

    The key constructs of the Meta Data Manager are: 

    • The MDM continuously monitors the SDS and storage 
    • The MDM provides system metadata and storage configuration information to the SDC 
    • There are three or five MDMs per system 
    • There is only one primary MDM at a time 
    • There are one or two secondary MDMs 
    • There are one or two tiebreakers 

     

    Figure 3.     MDM communication 

    Figure 3.   MDM communication

    The MDM topology is clustered by design. The primary MDM replication changes to system status synchronously. The MDM monitors the SDS status continuously and informs SDSs of changes to the system and MDM status, regarding instances and data layout. Device awareness can trigger rebuilds ahead of a potential failure.  

    Note: Temporary failures will not trigger a complete rebuild for a failed instance of the storage device if it comes back online.

Microsoft SQL Server 2022 multisubnet failover cluster on Dell APEX Block Storage for Public Cloud

  • A multisubnet failover cluster is a highly available solution that enables SQL Server 2022 instances to failover over various subnets. This functionality provides improved availability and disaster recovery capabilities for SQL Server deployments and is especially relevant when the APEX Block Storage cluster is configured across multiple-AZs, each one with its own subnet.

    In a multisubnet failover cluster, the SQL Server instances with APEX Block Storage multi-AZ configuration, can be set to automatically fail over in the event if one of the AZs has an outage.

    A simpler configuration can be deployed for APEX Block Storage, such as using a single AZ instead of multiple, and for SQL Server, such as using non-clustered configuration. The APEX Block Storage architecture for SQL Server 2022 multisubnet cluster on AWS cloud is used in this paper as a reference architecture for a more highly available solution.

    An APEX Block Storage deployment in AWS is set as a two-layer design, in which compute and storage instances are distinct. The two-layer design enables Amazon EC2 instances that are compute oriented for databases and application workloads to be configured and scaled separately from Amazon EC2 instances that are optimized for storage, providing customers with more flexibility.

Network architecture

  • The following figure shows the network architecture for a two-layer system that is deployed across multiple AZs in a single AWS region.

    Figure 4.        APEX Block Storage network architecture in AWS

    In this example, APEX Block Storage for AWS storage is deployed with one VPC (virtual private cloud) across three availability zones within the same AWS region for resiliency. For each availability zone, a separate private and public subnet is created to provide connectivity and routing across different availability zones. The public subnet contains resources that are accessible over the Internet and the private subnet contains the compute and storage resources.

    A network address translation (NAT) gateway is configured in the public routing table to enable access to the Amazon EC2 instances in public subnet over the Internet. Security groups are created for Amazon EC2 instances to provide an additional layer of security and control over inbound and outbound traffic at the subnet level.

Overview

  • In this solution, setup of the SQL Server 2022 failover cluster with APEX Block Storage benefits from the following elements that are particular to the configuration of this solution.

    • A highly available architecture that spans three Availability Zones.
    • A virtual private cloud (VPC) configured with public and private subnets, according to AWS best practices.
    • In the public subnets:
      • Managed network address translation (NAT) gateways to allow outbound Internet access for resources in the subnets.
    • In the private subnets:
      • Three Amazon EC2 instances running Microsoft Windows Server 2022 with SQL Server 2022. These instances are installed as nodes in a WSFC cluster in SQL Server FCI configuration across the Availability Zones. Each node contains an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) root volume.

    • SQL nodes are joined to an Active Directory domain which is also a DNS server to provide DNS name resolution.

    •        While creating a SQL cluster, an IP address gets assigned to each node. 

    • In a multisubnet cluster, SQL instance gets three different virtual IP addresses assigned - one virtual IP per IP subnet. This is to ensure that during failover there is at least one IP resource available to become the primary IP resource representing the cluster.
    • The configuration is required, because in multi-AZ and multisubnet cluster, failing over IP resource may not work properly across different subnets. Configuring multiple IPs with an OR operator allows any one of them to come online and bind to a cluster instance name.
    • The configuration may require you to create three different DNS hostname records in your DNS to enable client to obtain multiple addresses while making a DNS query.
    • SQL client connecting to the SQL instances receives three IP addresses from the DNS server. SQL client tries to connect each one of them one after the other and whichever node is active responds to the connection request and enables. 

    •        APEX Block Storage provides back-end shared storage for SQL Server cluster, which the FCI nodes require. This includes support for SCSI-3 reservations, whether SQL Server is deployed in a single or multi-AZ configuration. As a result, APEX Block Storage volumes can be used just like in an on-premises deployment to create Cluster Shared Volumes (CSV) disks, mount-points, or drive-letter type deployment in Windows Server Failover Cluster. CSVs employ a technique known as I/O Redirection. A particular node's ability to communicate with the underlying storage is maintained by the I/O Redirection feature, which helps to prevent storage connectivity failures from doing so. A host can still communicate with storage even though there is a storage failure by rerouting I/O over a cluster network to the coordinator node where the disk is mounted. When using CSV volumes, the coordinator node is the owner of the physical disk resources linked to the Volumes. The coordinator node synchronizes metadata with each of the physical hosts accessing the CSV when the CSV is changed.

Resourceful workload placement

  • Knowing where and how to implement efficient workloads is not always a simple task. It takes time, monitoring, and insights. It must also consider big islands of data, either in a database, or loosely stored in file systems. Historically, applications orbited around these large data stores. Fast forward to today, where the right data needs to land in the right place, at the right time. Being able to place data volumes close to the app that consumes them has now become as simple as replicating to the correct location, then mounting and consuming these volumes.

SLA reimagined

  • On average, cloud providers deliver anywhere between two to four nines of availability. With each “nine” there quickly adds exponential additional cost. Dell APEX Block Storage for Public Cloud pools together lower cost and lower durability volumes, all while presenting six “nines” of availability1 to your applications. By aggregating all the lower cost disk volumes, Dell APEX Block Storage can concentrate the collective performance of those pooled volumes to achieve a IOPs/dollar ratio that is not possible with native hyperscalers. 

    For a cloud first, or cloud smart, initiative (and there is not an appetite or a skills gap that exists to refactor apps), APEX Block Storage for Public Cloud can deliver without the cost of application refactoring and redesign, all while maintaining the most stringent on-premises SLAs. Combining the best of Dell software defined storage and cost-effective cloud agility can help satisfy the most mission-critical SLA requirements. 

    Dell APEX Block Storage provides thin provisioning of storage to a VM consumer and highly effective snapshots without limitations, when compared to native hyperscaler offerings.

SQL Server database tuning considerations

  • Consider the following tuning recommendations for the SQL Server 2022:

    • The general best practices for SQL Server high-performance and high-availability from on-premises are applicable to deployments in AWS. 
    • See the general best practices and recommendations for SQL Server clustering on Amazon EC2.
    • It is recommended to use four or more data files for high-performance SQL Server databases and store them on separate volumes. 
    • It is recommended to store database transaction logs on a separate volume than the data files for ease of performance monitoring and improved performance. 
    • It is recommended to place tempdb files in a separate volume or local NVMe persistent storage (if available) to avoid page contention.

TCO considerations

  • The Dell APEX Block Storage solution for public cloud offers an enterprise grade feature set that is not present with the public hyperscalers. It does so at a price point that over a short amount of time can be lower, dollar-per-I/O, than the public cloud offerings.  

    Dell APEX Block Storage can exceed the capacity and performance limitations of any public cloud disk type that costs less to run overall. The performance of an APEX Block Storage volume is directly proportional to the scale of the APEX Block Storage cluster created. Stated, bigger cluster = faster volumes. 

    When we look deeper into the total cost of ownership (TCO), note the core tenets of the APEX Block Storage solution: its operational and cost benefits. These core tenets are:  

    • Data mobility (with Async Replication) to one or many hyperscalers 
    • The need for a common platform on-premises and in any hyperscaler 
    • Thin provisioning options that the cloud native offers do not permit. 
    • On-premises, a customer can only deploy 2:1 overprovisioning with thin-provisioned volumes. 
    • Procurement time for hardware expansion can be long. 
    • Risk of running out of capacity due to long procurement. 
    • Customers can overprovision at rates at or exceeding 4:1 without any concern. This would not be an option for on-premises deployments. 
    • Scale up and scale down the storage cluster to fit current workload needs. Pay for only what you need, when you need it.

Testing and validation

  • This section provides a thorough description and explanation of the tests performed to verify the compatibility of the platform running SQL Server 2022 with Dell APEX Block Storage for Public Cloud. Database performance testing was carried out using the HammerDB benchmarking tool.

    HammerDB is the benchmarking and load testing program for the most popular databases. It is primarily concerned with schema building, data loading, and the simulation of any transactional or analytic activity. Due to these stress testing, valuable information from the environment is derived, such as hardware performance comparisons and software configurations.

    The test case shows the performance of a single SQL Server 2022 database instance and multiple SQL Server instances using APEX Block Storage volumes running in AWS. The APEX Block Storage pool uses AWS instance stores with four x 7.5 TB NVMe SSD drives on each Amazon EC2 instance. The number and size of NVMe SSD drives per instance are based on the AWS EC2 instance type selection. The NVMe SSD drive throughput is not shared with other instances, hence, no I/O reservation is necessary nor is I/O throttled. The total capacity of APEX Block Storage EC2 instances all together is 90 TB.

    A TPROC-C (TPCC-like, transactional) workload was simulated using the HammerDB benchmark test tool to assess the performance of SQL Server 2022 on Windows Server 2022.

    A TPROC-C database with 1000 GB of data per SQL Server 2022 instance was used for this reference architecture, and many virtual user tests were run at regular intervals to achieve higher IOPS. The HammerDB was run on a load generating EC2 Instance to generate real-time client/server situations. Multiple runs were carried out by simulating many virtual users.

    The goal of the tests was to demonstrate the following:

    • Single SQL Server database performance
    • Linear scaling test across multiple AWS AZ

Unique multi-AZ durability

  • The Dell APEX Block Storage self-healing architecture simplifies and increases the availability of infrastructure. It is designed to remain running even when it encounters failures. With fast rebuilds, Dell APEX Block Storage recovers rapidly from failures and keeps operating, without degrading performance or compromising availability. You can also extend this availability and configure it to protect your application availability across multiple availability zones. 

    Durability is defined by: 

    • Using Dell APEX Block Storage Fault Set architecture 
    • When spanning a single cluster across multiple availability zones or deploying into a single zone, the solution aggregates the capacity and performance. Having more instances means more performance and more resiliency. 
    • Retaining critical response time and IOPS performance properties 
    • Rapid reprotect from an instance failure, or even an AZ failure, with rapid rebuilds 

    Architecting fault sets, or fault domains, within the public hyperscalers provides unprecedented levels of storage availability that were previously unavailable in any public cloud platform. 

    • The unique multi-AZ architecture is defined by: 
    • The industry-first feature of a single cluster spanning multiple availability zones allows customers to set up non-replication-based fault tolerance across an entire hyperscaler region 
    • Scales linearly by federating instances 
    • No performance limitations 
    • Chooses your instance configurations based on the use case 
    • Protection across Availability Zones

Validate SQL Server 2022 multi-subnet failover cluster functionality

  • The main purpose of building a cluster is to ensure that the resources are available in case one of the nodes in the cluster goes down. To ensure that the resources are mapped to the secondary node, you need to manually move the cluster resources from the primary node to the secondary node.

    The roles are transferred from current active node SQLNODE-01 to SQLNODE-02 and then from SQLNODE-02 to SQLNODE-03.

    Connect to the Failover cluster manager. 

    Browse to Failover Cluster Manager > Roles > SQL Server (SQLDBFCI).

    Right-click the SQL Server cluster object running on SQLNODE-01 and move the Cluster Role. This provides a list of the other passive nodes in the cluster.

    Select node SQLNODE-02 and click OK.

    The cluster object role is now moved from SQLNODE-01 to SQLNODE-02 and the SQLNODE-01 has become a passive node.

    Similarly, move the roles from SQLNODE-02 to SQLNODE-03 and observe that the cluster object becomes online on SQLNODE-03.

    Select node SQLNODE-03 and click OK.

    The cluster object role is now moved from SQLNODE-02 to SQLNODE-03 and the SQLNODE-02 has become a passive node.
